rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Beyond the mentioned confounders, age and sex, multi-site MRI studies face the challenge of variability in imaging protocols, which can introduce site-related biases in the data. ComBat-GAM effectively harmonizes neuroimaging data by accounting for age and sex, in addition to mitigating site effects.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Z-score computed as: Z-score_icras = (y_icras - ŷ_irs) / sqrt(σ²_rs + σ²_icras), where y_icras is the observed volume, ŷ_irs is the normative model predicted volume for the patient's age and sex, and the denominator includes uncertainty from both the normative model (σ²_rs approximated from RMSE) and individual measurement (σ²_icras). Extreme deviations defined as |Z-score| > 1.96 (outside 95% confidence interval).
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper provides the explicit formula for calculating individual deviation Z-scores and defines the threshold for extreme deviations.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: For each patient and each region, we computed a Z-score to quantify the individual deviation from the normative value: Z-score_icras = (y_icras - ŷ_irs) / sqrt(σ²_rs + σ²_icras). Note that the uncertainty normalization term, σ²_rs, which assumes normality, is approximated using the reported RMSE model (see supplement in [18])... Red dashed lines at ±1.96 identify the 95% confidence interval. |Z-score| > 1.96 are considered extreme deviants.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed:
Answer: Using T1w and FLAIR MRI from 326 MS patients (460 scans) segmented with SynthSeg+ and SynthSeg-WMH, significant subcortical deviations were identified when compared to the CentileBrain normative model (37,407 healthy individuals). Key findings: (1) Thalamus showed consistent age-related increase in Z-score deviations across both hemispheres and sexes (p<0.05), with RMSE for left thalamus reaching 2038.95±112.1 for SynthSeg-WMH/T1w versus 1304±109.2 for SynthSeg+/FLAIR in males. (2) Putamen showed similar but non-significant increasing deviation trend. (3) For caudate, pallidum, and putamen, no significant differences were observed between segmentation approaches (ANOVA p>0.05). (4) For accumbens, amygdala, hippocampus, and thalamus, segmentation differences were primarily driven by the DL model choice rather than contrast (T1w vs FLAIR), except for thalamus where FLAIR with SynthSeg+ showed closest match to literature (K-S p=0.548). (5) SynthSeg-WMH generally produced volumes closer to literature reference values, particularly for regions affected by white matter lesions. (6) All regions except pallidum (in males) exhibited expected atrophy trends. (7) Amygdala showed atypical patterns, not presenting typical atrophy trajectory, consistent with known segmentation difficulties in this region. Results demonstrate feasibility of combining DL-based segmentation with normative modeling for MS progression characterization.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is a pilot/proof-of-concept study published in MICCAI 2024 Workshop proceedings (LNCS), representing early-stage work in applying normative modeling to MS. Study includes 460 scans from 326 unique MS patients, with longitudinal data available for OpenMSLong (20 patients with 2 timepoints), CHUV (36/41 patients longitudinal), and INsIDER (78/165 patients longitudinal). Imaging protocols varied substantially: field strengths 1.5T-3T; MSSEG2016 used 3D FLAIR/3D T1 with voxel sizes 0.47-1 × 0.47-1 × 0.9-1.25 mm; OpenMSLong used 3D FLAIR/2D T1 with 0.47×0.47×0.8 mm and 0.42×0.42×3.3 mm respectively; CHUV used 3D FLAIR/MP2RAGE at 1×1×1 and 1×1×1.2 mm; NIL used 3D FLAIR/MPRAGE at 0.69×0.66×0.66 and 0.71×0.66×0.66 mm; INsIDER used 3D FLAIR/MP2RAGE at 1×1×1 mm for both. The study references Ge et al. (2024) Lancet Digital Health for CentileBrain [18]; Royston & Altman (1994) for MFPR [38]; Billot et al. (2023) PNAS for SynthSeg+ [7]; Laso et al. (2024) for SynthSeg-WMH [29]; Fortin et al. (2018) Neuroimage for ComBat-GAM [16]; Rutherford et al. (2022) Nature Protocols for normative modeling framework [39]; and Keshavan et al. (2023) bioRxiv for Brain Charts for MS [26]. The study design is primarily cross-sectional analysis of deviations at each timepoint relative to normative trajectories, rather than true longitudinal modeling of within-subject change over time. Authors acknowledge potential bias from using T1w-derived literature reference values when validating FLAIR-based segmentations. Full list of 81 datasets in CentileBrain model not provided but referenced to Ge et al. 2024. Study received funding from CIBM and various sources including Hasler Foundation (NM), TRAIL/Walloon Region (MW), EUROSTAR E!113682 HORIZON2020 (AC). Several authors have industry relationships (consulting for Sanofi, Biogen, Merck, Roche, Novartis, GeNeuro, Actelion). The subcortical regions analyzed (7 bilateral structures = 14 ROIs) are standard outputs of FreeSurfer-based pipelines and CentileBrain model. SynthSeg+ and SynthSeg-WMH are both robust to resolution, contrast, and imaging artifacts, with the -WMH variant specifically designed to handle white matter hyperintensities/lesions common in MS, aging, and other conditions.
